description: Compare two web pages (for example a preview deployment and production) on the same simulated people and get Mimiq's call on which to ship. The same people see page A and page B. Mimiq's call combines a forecast, asked in both orders, with how the same people moved: clear, leaning, or too close to call (no pick). Returns the call, the reason in one sentence, how many people moved toward each page, each page's top objections, and a link to the report. Needs public URLs. Without a key, an agent also gets one free A/B test on up to 10 simulated people per version, while the daily free A/B allowance lasts. With a key, any size. On real web page tests the forecast did not beat the simplest guess in a pre-registered run: treat the call as a fast first read.

audience.description: Who the simulated people should be, in plain words, e.g. "startup founders in SF" or "parents shopping for kids toys". If omitted, Mimiq picks the likely audience from the content.

count.description: How many simulated people see both pages (default 10). Use 5 or more: from 5 people up, Mimiq reads who moved.

url_a.description: Page A, usually the current one (for example production).

url_b.description: Page B, usually the new one (for example a preview deployment).

name: mimiq.compare_urls
